newsitem.title: FRANCE: Italy to qualify for EU single currency - Veltroni.
newsitem.headline: Italy to qualify for EU single currency - Veltroni.

text.p: Italy will be among the initial group of European states to qualify for European monetary union, Italian Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni said on Thursday.
"Yes, absolutely yes," Veltroni said in a radio interview when asked whether Rome would qualify to join the single currency from 1999.
"We have returned to the European monetary system. I believe that our situation is not very different from that of the other (European) states," he told RTL radio.
Veltroni predicted that Italy would meet the monetary union requirement of a three percent or better ratio between the public deficit and Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
Under his government, inflation and interest rates had declined while the rate of economic growth had doubled, he said.

Critics of the centre-left government's budget, which aims to cut the 1997 deficit by 62.5 trillion lire, have predicted it will fail to get Italy into Europe's planned monetary union and that a supplementary budget will be needed to meet the deficit target.
